name: Seonix
summary: AI SEO tool that audits your site, suggests keywords and writes and schedules articles for you.
best_for: site owners who want a free audit and keyword ideas first, and small teams ready to pay for 30 AI articles a month on a single site
skip_if: your site is static with no publishing connection, you need several sites on one plan, or you want an article writer we have tested end to end
honest_knock: The AI writing is not on the free plan. The free scan covers a part of larger sites, 100 of our 285 pages. One issue pointed at an image URL instead of our page, and the tool promised fixes it cannot make on a static site. The refund does not apply once anything is generated.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Starter · per monthly, Starter is $49 a month, listed against a $100 regular price, or $470 a year instead of $1,200
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-13 on seonix.ai/pricing) Seonix has a free plan, a Starter plan and a custom Enterprise plan. Free costs $0 and covers a full website SEO audit, site health and page speed monitoring, an AI business profile, checks for broken links, duplicates and missing meta tags, an AI-search readiness check, and Search Console and GA4 analytics. Starter costs $49 a month, shown against a $100 regular price, or $470 a year shown against $1,200. It includes 1 website project, 30 AI articles a month, 50 AI edits a day, 5 AI cover images a day, auto-publish on a schedule, keyword research, the site audit and support. Enterprise is priced through sales and lists unlimited projects and content generation. The page mentions no free trial. First-time subscribers can ask for a refund within 14 days of the first payment, but only if nothing has been generated on the account. Monthly article limits do not roll over, and cancelling keeps access to the end of the paid period with no prorated refund. We did not buy Starter, so we do not know how the 30 articles read.

exit_test.what: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 13 November 2026 the session tested Seonix in two parts: the free plan on 13 November (onboarding, site scan, issues, keywords) and Starter on 14 November (integrations, planner, one AI article, billing). Nothing was connected or published. At 08:05 on 14 November the Overview showed STARTER and a banner to connect a channel to start publishing. The Content Plan showed 12 scheduled articles, one WILL WRITE article a day from 15 to 26 November, 3 of them as PILLAR. Seonix had by itself written a draft, Best Business Software for Small Business Without Overbuying (14 November, 1,664 words), which reused facts from our own site. Integrations says Pick one publishing destination: WordPress (plugin), REST API, Ghost (Admin API), Webflow (CMS collections), Wix and Shopify, with Notion coming soon. For a static site without a CMS the only route is the REST API: Connect Custom API says to publish articles to any site by exposing a REST endpoint that accepts the Seonix payload. One route lets an AI agent build it from a prompt plus a connect code; the manual route needs an endpoint that receives a POST for create and update, keyed on external_id, and a GET that lists the articles already on the site. It was not connected, because that would publish to the live site. The Calendar says Connect a channel to use the planner: auto-plan, drag and drop and slot scheduling work once a publishing channel is connected. Auto-publish was off with Every day recommended, and 19 of 216 topic clusters were ready. A vendor contact had advised connecting the site under Integrations first; the app says the same. Article: New article, Expert Article, topic Apollo.io pricing explained: what each plan really costs a small sales team, keyphrase Apollo pricing (commercial, 67), length 2,000. The first two clicks on Generate Content visibly did nothing: the network call to generate the article returned 409 without any message on screen. The third attempt, on a new form, started at about 08:09:50. The steps were Analyzing topic, Generating SEO title, Writing article content, Fact-checking and quality review and Preparing cover, with the screen saying This usually takes 30-60 seconds. The draft was ready at 08:16:52, about 7 minutes. The result, Apollo Pricing Explained for Small Sales Teams, has 2,076 words, 13 subheadings, Key takeaways and an FAQ, with SEO 90, Readability 87, AI answers 86 and the label Excellent; then Seonix is optimizing and Fixing the issues ran by itself. It names the plans Free, Basic, Professional and Organization, seats, credits that do not roll over, and Organization with minimum seats and annual payment, but it contains no price at all: 0 amounts, checked with a script. Our own dossier, re-verified on 1 October 2026, lists Basic 49, Professional 79 and Organization 119 dollars per seat a month billed annually, and 65, 99 and 149 monthly, with Organization needing at least 3 seats, which is 357 dollars a month. A pricing article without prices is safe, as nothing is invented, but it does not answer the search question. Not tested: connecting a real channel, publishing, Search Console and Analytics, Studio covers and cancelling. The draft stays unpublished in Seonix. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The first two Generate Content clicks failed silently with a 409, the article took about 7 minutes against 30 to 60 seconds on screen, and a static site can only connect through its own REST endpoint.

sessions.what: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 13 November 2026 we tested the Seonix free plan (onboarding, site scan, issues, keywords). On 14 November 2026 we tested Starter, which the vendor set to free for us until 12 January 2027, so no card was needed: integrations, the planner, one AI article and the billing page. Nothing was connected or published.
findings: Free plan: the site scan took under 10 seconds and gave a health score of 95 with 8 active issues. It checked 100 of our 285 sitemap pages. Generate Content said AI is not available on the Free plan.

Starter: the first two clicks on Generate Content did nothing on screen (the network call returned 409, with no message). The third attempt started at about 08:09:50 and the draft was ready at 08:16:52, about 7 minutes, against the 30 to 60 seconds shown on screen.

The draft, Apollo Pricing Explained for Small Sales Teams, has 2,076 words, 13 subheadings, key takeaways and an FAQ, and scored SEO 90, Readability 87 and AI answers 86 (Excellent). It contains no price at all (0 amounts, checked with a script), although our own dossier lists the plan prices. The scores do not check whether a pricing article answers the pricing question.

For a site without a CMS the only publishing route is the REST API option, which needs your own endpoint: a POST for create and update keyed on external_id, and a GET that lists the articles on the site. The calendar said auto-plan, drag and drop and slot scheduling work only once a channel is connected; auto-publish was off.
The Title Too Long issue lists 7 of our review pages and says Seonix will fix this itself. With no channel connected, nothing was fixed. Whether a connected channel fixes them was not tested.

Billing showed Starter at $49 a month, Active, renewing on 12 January 2027, with a Cancel subscription button and Save 20% for yearly billing. We saw no charge because the vendor set the plan to free. Tax and the final total are unknown because no checkout was opened.
Without our asking, Seonix had already planned 12 articles for 15 to 26 November and written a draft that reused facts from our own site.
